title: How do we find the highest common factor of five groups?
description: Five groups of numbers are each written as products of primes. Only the primes found in every number of a group are kept, each the smallest number of times it appears, and multiplying them gives that group's highest common factor. Each answer is then checked by dividing the numbers by it.
teaching_notes: One idea: keep only the primes present in every number of the group, each the smallest number of times, then multiply. Ask the class which prime is shared in the second group before the working is shown. Watch for students who keep a prime that is missing from one of the numbers.

video_script.why: The child has seen the highest common factor found from prime products for two numbers and now meets five groups, one of them with three numbers.
video_script.substitution: For each group write the prime products, keep the primes found in every number the smallest number of times, and multiply.
video_script.anchor: Five groups of numbers in a column: 24 and 180; 42, 75 and 24; 240 and 378; 400 and 2500; 300 and 800.
video_script.payoff_line: The highest common factors are twelve, three, six, one hundred and one hundred

final_answer.spoken: twelve, three, six, one hundred and one hundred

never_show: a group answer before its own step
maths_rules: 24 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 and 180 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 5; smaller counts: 2 twice, 3 once; HCF = 2 × 2 × 3 = 12
42 = 2 × 3 × 7, 75 = 3 × 5 × 5, 24 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3; only 3 is in all three, once; HCF = 3
video_script.design: One idea: keep the primes found in every number, the smallest number of times. The five groups stay in the anchor band all video and each step lights one group. The check divides each number by its answer.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>We must find the highest common factor of the numbers in five groups.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>First, twenty four with one hundred eighty. Second, forty two, seventy five and twenty four.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Third, two hundred forty with three hundred seventy eight. Fourth, four hundred with two thousand five hundred. Fifth, three hundred with eight hundred.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>How do we find each highest common factor?

beats.on_screen: the five groups stay still; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: cards: a prime missing from one number is crossed out; for a shared prime the smallest count is the most every number can hold

marks.m1: a card shows a prime missing from one number, crossed out

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>A prime that is missing from even one number cannot be shared.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>For a shared prime, the smallest count is the most every number can hold.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>We work the same way as the example in your book.

marks.m1: the given line is written in the working band

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, five groups of numbers.

beats.on_screen: To find: the HCF of each group

marks.m1: the find line is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find the highest common factor of each group.

beats.on_screen: Step 1, first group: 24 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3; 180 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 5; keep 2 twice and 3 once; HCF = 2 × 2 × 3 = 12

marks.m3: two 2s and one 3 are lit and HCF = 2 × 2 × 3 = 12 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, take the first group. Twenty four is two times two times two times three.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>One hundred eighty is two times two times three times three times five.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Keep two twos and one three, and multiply them to get twelve.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, second group: 42 = 2 × 3 × 7; 75 = 3 × 5 × 5; 24 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3; only 3 is in all three; HCF = 3

marks.m3: only the 3 in each product is lit and HCF = 3 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, the second group has three numbers. Forty two is two times three times seven. Seventy five is three times five times five.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Twenty four is two times two times two times three.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Only three is in all of them, once each, so the answer is three.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, third group: 240 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 5; 378 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 7; keep 2 once and 3 once; HCF = 2 × 3 = 6

marks.m3: one 2 and one 3 are lit and HCF = 2 × 3 = 6 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, two hundred forty has four twos, a three and a five.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Three hundred seventy eight has one two, three threes and a seven.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Keep one two and one three, which multiply to six.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, fourth group: 400 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 5 × 5; 2500 = 2 × 2 × 5 × 5 × 5 × 5; keep 2 twice and 5 twice; HCF = 2 × 2 × 5 × 5 = 100

marks.m3: two 2s and two 5s are lit and HCF = 2 × 2 × 5 × 5 = 100 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, four hundred has four twos and two fives.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Two thousand five hundred has two twos and four fives.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Keep two twos and two fives, which multiply to one hundred.

beats.on_screen: Step 5, fifth group: 300 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 × 5; 800 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 5 × 5; keep 2 twice and 5 twice; HCF = 2 × 2 × 5 × 5 = 100

marks.m3: two 2s and two 5s are lit and HCF = 2 × 2 × 5 × 5 = 100 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step five, three hundred has two twos, a three and two fives.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Eight hundred has five twos and two fives.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Again keep two twos and two fives, which multiply to one hundred.

marks.m1: the word check is written above the divisions
marks.m2: the divisions for the first and second groups are written, all whole numbers
marks.m3: the divisions for the third, fourth and fifth groups are written, all whole numbers

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step six, check that each answer divides every number in its group.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Twelve divides twenty four and one hundred eighty. Three divides forty two, seventy five and twenty four.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Six divides two hundred forty and three hundred seventy eight. One hundred divides all four of the other numbers.

marks.m1: the five answers are written and boxed
marks.m2: each answer is tied to its group

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The highest common factors are twelve, three, six, one hundred and one hundred.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Each one is the product of the primes shared by its group.
